title: AbstainGNN: Teaching Graph Neural Networks to Abstain for Graph Classification

problem.claim: Graph neural networks for graph classification are typically forced to make predictions under high uncertainty or unknown conditions, which can produce unreliable downstream decisions.

gap.claim: Existing graph neural networks and heuristic abstention methods do not provide the proposed integrated, theoretically characterized approach to abstention for graph classification.

contributions.claim: AbstainGNN is a framework for graph classification with abstention that enables GNNs to reject uncertain predictions.
The framework characterizes the trade-off between classification errors and rejection costs from a PAC-Bayesian generalization perspective and derives a unified learning objective.
The authors develop a two-stage training strategy consisting of predictive-function warm-start and abstention-function calibration.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe AbstainGNN as a novel and theory-driven framework for graph classification with abstention.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five benchmark datasets are reported to show that AbstainGNN outperforms existing abstention methods and achieves superior classification performance at the same rejection rates.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph classification is important, and GNN advances have improved its performance.
GNNs can be unreliable when required to predict under uncertainty or unknown conditions.
AbstainGNN models prediction and abstention functions, theoretically analyzes error-rejection trade-offs, and uses a two-stage training strategy.
The authors report favorable results on five benchmark datasets at matched rejection rates.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five benchmark datasets.
The abstract does not report quantitative performance results or rejection-rate values.
The abstract does not describe implementation details, baselines, or computational costs.
